items.label: Published sales anyone can attribute
items.note: Every result is reach, trends or sell-outs. Not one figure traces back to sales

footnote: Sources: Digitaling (Mar 2024, Jun 2024, Jun 2025), 21st Century Business Herald, China.com, Jiemian, Xin Caijing. All results self-reported
notes: What peers have done. Drinks, tea and dairy brands already have a full playbook at live shows: naming rights, drink stations, tie-in combos, co-branded packs, buy-a-product-win-a-ticket and scan-to-win. Hushang Ayi ran a two-cup combo with Jason Zhang's 2024 tour in more than 700 stores across 12 cities and, by company and platform figures, sold 10,000 in ten minutes, while its ordering system also crashed. Zhanma named every drink station at Strawberry Festival Xinjiang. The nearly 80,000 fans were the whole festival, not people reached by the brand. Changqing's co-branded pack let shoppers win tickets by buying yogurt, with no results disclosed. Yili Xujinhuan and Yanghe reported impressions and video views. The key point is that published results are almost all self-reported impressions, trending topics and sell-outs. We could not find a single published, attributable figure for sales or repeat purchase. That is the gap this plan closes: every contact has to count back to sales.
